title: service-window-notice-patterns-and-tf-module-annotations
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc collects: 1) customer-facing notice patterns for scheduled service windows and upgrades for VPC/on-prem customers, 2) compact SLO/SLA language and incident classification guidance to include in notices, and 3) annotated Terraform module notes and a short upgrade checklist engineers should attach to customer communications. Goal is a single place we can copy/paste from for consistent, low-friction communication and repeatable upgrade ops across private deployments.

Audience segments and channels:
- Primary recipients: production contacts (technical and ops) at the customer, named slack/jira integration endpoints, and security/compliance approvers when relevant.
- Channels: email (primary), account-specific console banner, dedicated support ticket update, optional Slack/Teams webhook notification (if integrated), and SMS for high-impact windows (only if agreed).

Timing cadence (recommended):
- Advance notification: 14 days (major upgrades/backwards-incompatible changes). For minor patch/security-only updates 72 hours is acceptable.
- Reminder cadence: 7 days -> 24 hours -> 1 hour before start -> start/completion notices.
- Post-update: Postmortem within 5 business days if incidents occurred; otherwise short confirmation + compatibility notes within 48 hours.

SLO/SLA language (short snippets to reuse):
- High-level SLO summary (customer-facing): "Our platform aims for 99.95% availability of inference endpoints measured per calendar month. Availability excludes planned maintenance announced at least 72 hours in advance and emergency maintenance required for security or compliance."
- What we measure (SLIs): 1) 95th percentile inference latency for common sequence lengths, 2) successful request rate (HTTP 2xx), 3) model load/serve readiness.
- Exclusion language: "Planned service windows, agreed rollback operations, and failure modes caused by customer-managed network or infrastructure are excluded from SLA calculations."

Impact classifications (for notice templates):
- Low (Informational): Configuration-only changes, no service disruption expected.
- Medium (Degraded): Rolling upgrades with transient instance restarts; best-effort zero-downtime but brief 1-3 minute token delays possible per request.
- High (Interruption): Single-region maintenance where short endpoint unavailability is expected (we provide fallback routes if configured).

Subject line patterns (pick one):
- [Action Required] Scheduled service window for {customer_name} — {YYYY-MM-DD}
- [Info] Planned infra update — expected low impact — {YYYY-MM-DD}
- [Urgent] Security patch window — may cause brief interruptions — {YYYY-MM-DD}

Short email template (concise, technical recipients):
Subject: [Action Required] Scheduled service window for {customer_name} — {StartDate}
Hi {PrimaryContact},

We will perform a scheduled platform update for your private deployment on {StartDate} at {StartTime} {TZ}. This upgrade targets the serving runtime and operator-managed infra and uses a rolling strategy across nodes.

Expected impact: Medium — rolling restarts of worker nodes. Individual inference requests may experience brief latency spikes (~1-3 minutes) while affected hosts drain. No model snapshot or data migration is required.

Pre-steps you should run (optional):
- Confirm network ACLs allow outbound to our control-plane endpoints: {control_plane_urls}.
- Take any internal config backups you require; we will not modify customer-provisioned data stores.

If you have an agreed blackout window or require a more narrow maintenance period, reply with your preferred window within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference — Private Deployments

Verbose email template (customer success + compliance audiences):
Subject: Planned service window for {customer_name} — {StartDate} (details enclosed)
Greeting {Customer Team},

Summary: We will apply v{new_version} of the serving runtime to your cluster on {StartDate} at {StartTime} {TZ}. This release includes security fixes (CVE-YYYY-XXXX), performance improvements for batching, and an optional config toggle (enable_kv_cache=true) that reduces cold-start tokens by ~12%.

What to expect: Rolling node restarts over an estimated {duration_hours} hours. Endpoint availability is expected to remain within your SLA for most traffic patterns; you may notice brief request retry behavior for specific long-poll requests.

Escalation & contacts:
- Primary account engineer: {owner_name} — {owner_email}
- On-call infra lead: {oncall_name} — pager: {oncall_pager}
- Security contact: security@redwood.ai (for customers with SOC2 addendum)

Rollback: We will monitor for increased error rates and will execute an automated rollback to the previous runtime in the event of a severity >= P1 impact. The rollback procedure is tested internally and typically completes within 20–40 minutes.

Compliance notes: All changes are applied by our operator with audit logs stored in the customer-managed logging bucket (if configured) or our control-plane audit service. We will provide log excerpts on request.

Terraform module annotation guide (engineer-facing snippet to attach to notices):
- Purpose: show customers the exact module and variable changes so reviewers can trace what changed in their IaC. Use this for any upgrade that touches module inputs or requires module-version changes.

Example annotated snippet to include in customer ticket (HCL):

# BEFORE
module "redwood_inference" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private-deploy"
  version = "v1.2.0"
  enable_blue_green = false
  instance_type = "g4dn.xlarge"
}

# AFTER (we will apply operator-side; include as traceability)
module "redwood_inference" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private-deploy"
  version = "v1.3.0"  # bump contains security fixes + rolling upgrade support
  enable_blue_green = true # enable blue/green switch to reduce customer-facing interruptions
  instance_type = "g5.xlarge"       # optional perf bump, requires capacity validation
  notes = "applied by Redwood operator on {StartDate}; see change-id: {change_id}"
}

Recommended short changelog for customers (bullet list):
- v1.3.0: CVE mitigation, rolling upgrade support, blue/green toggle, improved batch kernel selection.
- Why this matters: reduces end-user tail latency during restarts and patches a kernel-level security exposure.

Engineer checklist (pre-apply):
1) Confirm backup snapshot exists for control-plane metadata (S3/GCS snapshot id: {snapshot_id}).
2) Validate module version compatibility with node pool AMI/container runtime.
3) Smoke test orchestration in staging with traffic replay of representative workload.
4) Run terraform plan and attach plan output to the ticket.
5) Schedule a canary batch (10% traffic) for first 30 minutes; monitor error rates and latency.
6) Prepare quick-rollback terraform apply to previous module version if severity threshold crossed.

Post-upgrade validation script (high level):
- Verify all nodes report serve-ready in the control-plane (api:/clusters/{id}/nodes -> status == READY).
- Run 50 synthetic inference requests across endpoints and assert 95% success and 95th latency below threshold.
- Confirm model versions & KV cache primed for top-5 models by recent traffic.

Customer-facing FAQ snippets (append to notice):
Q: Will my model weights be changed?
A: No. We do not modify customer model artifacts. We only update the serving runtime and optional operator-managed infra.

Q: Can you perform the work outside my business hours?
A: Yes — provide your preferred window in your reply. For high-impact windows we will ask for an explicit approval.

Q: What happens if something goes wrong?
A: We will notify immediately, execute a rollback if a P1 threshold is reached, and follow with a postmortem. Our SREs will remain engaged until service stabilizes.

Banner / console blurb (short):
Planned update: Redwood operator will upgrade serving runtime to v{new_version} on {StartDate} {StartTime}. Rolling restarts expected; see ticket {ticket_id} for details.

Sample Slack webhook payload (plain text):
- Title: Planned update for {customer_name}: serve runtime v{new_version}
- Body: Start {StartDate} {StartTime} {TZ} — rolling restarts — contact {owner_email} for questions.

Escalation thresholds (suggested):
- P2 -> if error rate > 1% for 30 minutes across 5+ endpoints escalate to infra oncall.
- P1 -> if >= 5% of requests fail for > 15 minutes or tenant unreachable escalate to company incident procedure.

Long-term notes for module authors (docs to include in repo):
- Always include a clear semantic-versioned module tag and short changelog entry when introducing a behavioral change.
- Expose an "upgrade_strategy" variable (values: rolling | blue_green | immediate) and document the expected customer impact for each.
- Provide a lightweight smoke test harness users/operators can run post-apply.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing templates):
- Do we require explicit customer approval for minor (non-security) runtime bumps? default: no for <72h notice, yes for major semantics changes.
- Should we standardize on 14 days for all major changes or provide per-customer tiers based on contract?

Next steps:
- Iterate with CS legal for compliant wording for customers with strict change control.
- Attach a short terraform "plan" artifact to every customer ticket that includes the module diff (automated via GH Action).
- Pilot these templates with three low-risk private customers during Q1 and capture feedback.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2025-02-18: added Terraform annotated examples and updated cadence recommendations (Ethan Rivera).

End of doc.
